title: Double-time writing, Dizzy's blues for Eckstine, and thinking in two keys
summary: Dizzy shows him double-time rhythms and the flatted-fifth idea of playing in two keys at once, which he still uses.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: And then, just writing certain rhythms. Dizzy actually showed me how to write double-time, which I hadn't been exposed to. He did a lot of double time rhythms in tunes...in a ballad where you would actually be playing in two or three tempos at the same time. The basic beat would be a ballad, but the melodic line or the rhythmic line sometimes would be

double that of the basic beat.
And so, things like that, that I hadn't been exposed to, that I had heard before, but I just didn't comprehend how it was done. In playing some of his writings and with some of his coaching, these things all came to light. I wish I could remember that blues that he wrote for Billy Eckstine. It was in back of the single that they did with Budd Johnson's arrangement, "I Stay In The Mood For You," and that's a number on the back of that that Dizzy Gillespie wrote, the blues, that I really like much better... Of course, both of them were fine arrangements. But this particular one, I can't remember the name of it, but it's really a very exciting arrangement. And things like certain rhythms that he had in the introduction for "Round Midnight"... Dizzy always seemed to think in terms of what seemed then complex rhythms.

And he also used to talk about playing in two keys at one time, which I learned later was the flatted fifth idea, which results in me having a certain concept, and every musician has his little thing that you figure out for your own advantage... When I'm playing in one key, I always think of myself as playing in two keys. For example, if I'm playing in the key of D-flat, five flats, I also think in the key of G. Or if I'm playing in the key of C, I can think in the key of F-sharp or G-flat. These are things that I use to my own advantage.
In other words, I think of these two keys as being the same key. These are things that I actually learned from Dizzy orally -- he'd tell me one thing or another.
